amira: FYI ran nsys on the prod shard during the slow cold starts. Seeing big compile stalls when Triton does per-kernel compilation — ~150-250ms per compile for some fused attention kernels. nsys trace attached, timeline shows repeated spikes when kernel_cache misses.

kevin: thanks — can you paste the kernel names? is this on A100 or H100?

amira: H100s in dedicated pool. Example kernels:
```
triton_fused_attn_bwd_128x64x32
triton_matmul_small_32x32
triton_layernorm_fwd
```
trace snippet shows compile time blocks labeled "jit_compile" interleaved with execute. Warmup sequence:
```
[0.001s] launch matmul -> jit_compile (0.18s)
[0.19s] execute matmul
[0.20s] launch fused_attn -> jit_compile (0.22s)
```

rahul: hmm sounds like kernel cache isn't being hit across shards. We hash kernel config by (model_id, seqlen, type). If batch shaping varies, cache keys differ. Maybe different batch dims? Did you enable "strip_batch_axis" option?

amira: Not explicitly. Batches coming in are 1/2/4/8 depending on traffic. Also saw cache eviction events in our logs: `kernel_cache.evicted=1` around the same time as first requests after deploy.

julia: Could this be due to per-container tempdir for Triton compiles? We mount /tmp per-pod and it's ephemeral on restart, so compiles are repeated after pod recycle.

kevin: good point — our autoscaler spins up fresh pods frequently at low traffic. Two mitigations: pre-warm at deploy (compile-on-start) or central persistent cache stored on shared FS (nfs / ceph). Pre-warm script could call our `compile_kernel` admin endpoint.

amira: ran a quick experiment: added `--precompile=all` in the container entrypoint. Cold start p95 latency dropped from 820ms -> 320ms for initial request (still costly but better). But compile step increased deploy time by ~3s.

rahul: tradeoff. Another approach: micro-cache of compiled kernels per node across containers (daemonset) to avoid recompile even if containers restart. Or persist Triton cache to local NVMe via hostPath.

amira: also interesting: perfetto shows many small kernels being launched repeatedly due to batching heuristic: when batch_size < threshold we don't fuse, causing many more kernel variants. Suggest tuning batching heuristic to favor fusion up to batch 8.

kevin: can you open a PR with the perf logs and the suggested heuristic change (tuning param `fusion_min_batch=4`)? we'll run A/B on staging.

amira: will do. I'll also attach the nsys flame and the raw perf logs to the ticket. Tagging perf-bot for trace retention :perf: 

perf-bot: saved trace 1771200456 for 30d (nsys://traces/1771200456.nsys)

julia: +1 on doing persistent cache on nodes; infra to evaluate security/ops implications. Also we should add a regression test in eng-runtime CI that runs cold-start profile and fails if compile time > 200ms for critical kernels.

kevin: ok — action items: amira PR w/ logs + heuristic change, rahul prototype daemonset cache, infra to eval hostPath/FS options. I'll create a todo issue.

amira: thanks. attaching quick commands i used:
```
nsys profile --output=1771200456 --trace-fork=true --capture-range=cpu nvtx -- python -m perf_test --model gpt-small
```

(End of thread)
